summary: The note covers early timekeeping devices, focusing on the origins of sundials. It states that the oldest known sundial is from Egypt, dating to about 1500 BC in the 19th Dynasty, and was discovered in the Valley of the Kings in 2013. It also explains that sundials descend from shadow clocks, the first devices used to measure parts of a day, and notes that ancient Egyptian obelisks from about 3500 BC are among the earliest shadow clocks.
one_line: Overview of early timekeeping, tracing sundials to shadow clocks and the oldest known sundial from Egypt.
